fields.h1: Build a Pet Adoption Form That Tracks Every Application
fields.hero_description: Build a pet adoption form that asks each applicant only what applies and saves every application to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Handles Before Anyone Adopts
fields.features_subheading: A pet adoption form collects each applicant's home and pet history, then moves the application through checks to a signed contract.
fields.feature_1:
Every application on the animal's record

The applicant picks an animal from your current adoptable list, and the application lands on that animal's record. Staff open the animal and see everyone who applied, oldest first.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that follow the last answer

An applicant who rents gets questions about the landlord, and one with pets at home gets questions about their vet. Everyone else skips both and finishes a shorter form.
fields.feature_3:
Review steps with a named owner

Each application moves through steps you define, such as a vet reference or a site visit. When a volunteer marks a step done, the next one opens for the person who owns it.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts to the foster, not a shared inbox

A new application emails the foster who cares for that animal, or posts in a Slack channel you pick. A reminder goes out when a step sits untouched past the days you set.
fields.feature_5:
The contract signed on any screen

The adopter signs your adoption contract on a phone or a tablet, even at an event table. The app saves the signature with the application and closes the animal's listing.
fields.feature_6:
Code and records you keep

Export the app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Every application, reference note, and signed contract stays in a database you own, filed under its animal.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Adoption Teams, Four Different Checks
fields.tab_content_1:
Renters get two questions no owner sees

Larchmere Dog Rescue asks every applicant whether they own or rent. Ezequiel Hollenbeck rents, and the form asks him two more questions: his landlord's name and phone number, and whether his lease allows a 62-pound dog like Moose. His application goes to Moose's foster, Maribel Pembleton, as an email.
fields.tab_content_2:
No meet-and-greet until the vet confirms

Sorrel Street Cat Rescue checks a vet reference for any applicant with pets. Florencia Abernethy lists 2 cats and their clinic. Volunteer Thaddeus Ruelle confirms with the clinic that both cats are vaccinated and marks the reference done. The app emails Florencia a link to book a meet-and-greet with Pepper.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each application under 2 acres waits for a visit

Cinder Hill Horse Rescue asks how many acres of pasture an applicant has for the horse. Its own rule sends any application under 2 acres to a site visit before review. Leopold Kaplan reports 1.5 acres. His application is marked Site visit, and the 5 others this week go straight to review.
fields.tab_content_4:
Signed at the event, adopted in the app

Lantern Bay Animal Shelter brings its adoptable cats to a Saturday adoption event at a pet supply store. Yusra Whitcombe, approved earlier that week, signs the adoption contract for Clementine on a volunteer's phone. The app saves her signature with the application and changes Clementine from Available to Adopted.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pet Adoption Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps turn the application you use today into a pet adoption form that tracks each application, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Name each review step and its owner
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Load the animals you have now
fields.howto_step_1_des: Read the application you use today and note what each answer changes about a placement. Keep the questions that decide one, such as housing and the pets already at home, and drop any question whose answer nobody reads.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide which answers open more questions. A renter gets the landlord questions and an applicant with pets gets the vet questions. Everyone else moves straight on, and a first-time owner with no pets finishes a shorter form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the steps an application passes through before approval, such as the vet reference, a landlord call, a site visit, and the meet-and-greet. Give each step one owner, and note which steps apply only to some applications.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Load the animals in your care and record each one's status and the foster who looks after it. Applicants pick from this list. Each application is then filed under one animal and reaches that animal's foster.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt to Emergent that covers the questions with their follow-up rules and the review steps with their owners. Emergent builds the form with the database behind it, and you change a question or a step later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste in your adoption contract so an approved adopter can sign it on a phone or tablet. Then decide who hears about what: new applications go to the animal's foster, and a stalled step sends its owner a reminder.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as three made-up applicants: an owner with no pets, a renter with a cat, and someone with 2 dogs at home. Check that each lands at the right step, then publish on its own link or your custom domain (included in Emergent, uses credits).

faq_plan.q: What is a pet adoption form?
faq_plan.a: A pet adoption form is the application a shelter or rescue asks someone to complete before they adopt an animal. It records who the applicant is, where the animal would live, and which pets are already in the home. Staff read those answers to decide on a placement.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pet adoption form?
faq_plan.a: List the questions that decide a placement and every check an application passes before approval. Describe both in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the form with its review steps on a database that holds every application.

faq_plan.q: What questions should an adoption application form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with contact details, the animal they want, whether they own or rent, and who lives in the home. Then ask how many hours a day the animal would be alone and what happened to any past pets. An adoption application form needs little more than that to support a placement decision.

faq_plan.q: What should a pet adoption form template ask renters?
faq_plan.a: Ask renters who their landlord is, how to reach them, and whether the lease allows the animal they want, including any size or breed limit written into it. Put those in your pet adoption form template as questions only renters see. The check runs the other way from a rental application form, where the landlord screens the tenant.

faq_plan.q: How do I offer a paper copy of my pet adoption form?
faq_plan.hint: How to put a pet adoption form in the paper?
faq_plan.a: Print the same questions in the same order as the online form, with the follow-ups grouped under a heading for renters and one for current pet owners. Post that pet adoption form PDF next to the online link. When a paper application comes in, a volunteer types it into the app and it joins the same review steps.

faq_plan.q: Can one pet adoption form work for both dogs and cats?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask which animal the applicant wants first, and let that answer decide the rest. A dog applicant sees questions about the yard and walks, while a cat applicant sees questions about indoor space. One form beats separate pet adoption forms per species because every application lands in one list. In an app built with Emergent, you add a species, such as rabbits, by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Should a pet adoption form ask about income or credit?
faq_plan.a: You can leave both off. An adoption is not a loan, and a question about whether the applicant has planned for food and vet costs tells you more about the home. Income and credit questions belong on a credit application form, where a business decides whether to extend credit.

faq_plan.q: Which references should a pet adoption form collect?
faq_plan.a: Collect the applicant's vet clinic when they have pets now and the landlord when they rent. Add one personal reference who has seen them with animals, with a name and phone number. Record the result of each call on the application, along with who made it and the date.

faq_plan.q: What happens after someone submits a pet adoption form?
faq_plan.a: The application moves through the review steps the shelter or rescue sets, such as reference calls or a meet-and-greet, and ends in an approval or a decline. Show applicants those steps on the confirmation screen and email them as each one finishes. An app built with Emergent has no response caps, and the form stays open through a busy adoption weekend.

faq_plan.q: Can a rescue run its pet adoption form and transport driver sign-ups in one app?
faq_plan.a: The app Emergent builds can run both. Next to the adoption form, it can hold a sign-up for volunteers who drive animals to vet visits or new homes, with its own fields and reviewers. If you also hire paid drivers, a driver application form collects their license and driving history.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Pet Adoption Form That Tracks Every Application'; hero 'Build a pet adoption form that asks each applicant only what applies and saves every application to a database you own.' covers the whole application job, not one feature; how-to description is one sentence with the primary.

intent.evidence: AMBER angle (rescues building their own application) carried throughout: questions that decide a placement (step 01, FAQ 3), renter and vet follow-ups (tab 1, FAQ 4, FAQ 8), review steps to a signed contract (tabs 2-4); template and PDF searchers served by FAQ 4 and FAQ 5.

specificity.evidence: Rescue vocabulary throughout: foster, vet reference, site visit, meet-and-greet, 'whether his lease allows a 62-pound dog like Moose', 'any application under 2 acres to a site visit'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences that say what happens: 'The applicant picks an animal from your current adoptable list', 'Larchmere Dog Rescue asks every applicant whether they own or rent.'

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; QC Q-checks clean. Repeated renter/vet follow-up idea recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail ('the 5 others this week go straight to review', 'oldest first'); meta description wording and feature 4 heading recorded as notes.

truth.evidence: Emergent sentences map to claims_used (prompt-build, alerts 'emails the foster ... or posts in a Slack channel', e-signature-capture with no legal-validity claim, code-export 'on paid plans', custom-domain 'included in Emergent, uses credits', no-caps, free-start); thresholds framed as each rescue's own rule ('Its own rule sends any application under 2 acres'); no veterinary advice; table from library; tab numbers agree (1.5 acres, 5 others, 2 cats).

distinct.evidence: Animal-record filing, foster routing and the adoption-event contract are specific to rescues; sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors (rental application form, credit application form, driver application form).

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first ('Yes. Ask which animal the applicant wants first'); hub link in item 2; secondaries read naturally; moat lines in FAQ 6 and FAQ 9 from approved claims. FAQ 10 framing recorded as a note.
